biomarkers.name: Cytogenetics (karyotype)
biomarkers.clinical_use: IPSS-R cytogenetic risk groups are based on marrow karyotype (very good: -Y, del(11q); good: normal, del(5q), del(12p), del(20q), double including del(5q); intermediate; poor; very poor: complex, monosomal)

biomarkers.name: Somatic mutation panel (SF3B1, TET2, ASXL1, DNMT3A, SRSF2, U2AF1, TP53, EZH2, RUNX1, STAG2, others)
biomarkers.clinical_use: IPSS-M (molecular) incorporates recurrent myeloid gene mutations and refines IPSS-R risk. Multihit/bi-allelic TP53 = adverse. SF3B1 is associated with a favourable phenotype, especially in MDS with ring sideroblasts, but prognosis depends on overall disease context

biomarkers.name: IPSS-R / IPSS-M risk scores
biomarkers.clinical_use: Guides therapy intensity and transplant referral

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Bone marrow dysplasia (≥10% dysplastic cells) in a single lineage (erythroid, granulocytic, or megakaryocytic) with peripheral cytopenia; dysplasia may involve one lineage while cytopenia need not strictly be limited to the same lineage
histomorphological_subtype.grading: IPSS-R / IPSS-M risk scores; not morphologically graded

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Clonal haematopoietic stem cell disorder; autoimmune complications and inflammatory dysregulation are increasingly recognised
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Bone marrow architecture with dyspoiesis; often normocellular or hypercellular for age but occasionally hypocellular (hypoplastic MDS overlap)

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Haematopoietic stem/progenitor cell with clonal expansion producing ineffective haematopoiesis with single-lineage dysplasia
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Dysplastic differentiation in a single lineage (erythroid, granulocytic, or megakaryocytic) with peripheral cytopenia; represents chronic ineffective haematopoiesis with maintained differentiation but abnormal maturation
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: MDS represents clonal haematopoiesis with lineage-restricted dysplasia; progression to higher-grade MDS or AML involves acquisition of additional driver alterations including TP53, RUNX1, and other recurrent myeloid mutations
